record_identity.title: More than 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis stopped in live Wuhan traffic during a system failure

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 31 March 2026 Apollo Go Wuhan fleet outage
incident_identity.date_basis: Wuhan traffic police reported that calls began at approximately 20:57 on 31 March 2026; Reuters and AIID record the same occurrence.

summary: A reported system failure caused more than 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis in Wuhan to stop in live traffic, including on elevated roads, stranding passengers until police and company personnel responded. Authorities reported that passengers exited safely and no injuries were recorded. The technical root cause remains under investigation in the public record.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters reports Wuhan traffic police described the event as a system failure affecting more than 100 Apollo Go vehicles. AIID Incident 1460 preserves the same occurrence and affected-system entities. Public evidence establishes correlated fleet-wide stoppage and passenger stranding but not the specific failing component.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates a material correlated-failure mode in embodied autonomous infrastructure: a shared system failure can simultaneously immobilise a large fleet in live road environments. Without a confirmed root cause, VIGIL does not infer whether the mechanism involved central control, communications, cloud infrastructure, fleet orchestration or vehicle-local software.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This materially broadens VIGIL into embodied autonomy and fleet-level systemic dependency, providing a counterweight to chatbot-centric incidents and evidence for future continuity, fail-safe and correlated-dependency governance work.
assessment_boundaries: The specific technical root cause and failing component are not established in the reviewed public evidence.
VIGIL does not infer that vehicles failed to enter a particular designed fallback state unless the relevant design requirement is independently established.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: More than 100 autonomous taxis stopped in live traffic and stranded passengers until responders and company personnel intervened.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: At least 100 Apollo Go vehicles across Wuhan and their passengers and surrounding road users; no injuries were reported.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The failure created a material road-safety and transport disruption across a commercial autonomous fleet but was time-bounded and resolved without reported injury.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: Wuhan police reported more than 100 affected vehicles; some passengers were reportedly stranded for extended periods, with no reported injuries.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: The specific technical root cause and failing component are not established in the reviewed public evidence. No injuries were reported. VIGIL does not infer that vehicles failed to enter a particular designed fallback state unless the relevant design requirement is independently established.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S3 rather than S2 is appropriate because no injury, persistent service loss or severe downstream harm is established. S3 rather than S4 is appropriate because simultaneous immobilisation of more than 100 autonomous vehicles in live traffic materially disrupted a safety-critical embodied service.
